lines.raw: Two ways to get Part D.

lines.raw: **PDP** (Prescription Drug Plan). What it is: A standalone drug-only plan. Used with: Original Medicare. Robert: 2022 to 2023.
lines.say: P D P (Prescription Drug Plan). What it is: A standalone drug-only plan. Used with: Original Medicare. Robert: 2022 to 2023.

lines.raw: **MA-PD** (Medicare Advantage Prescription Drug plan). What it is: Drug cover built into an MA plan. Used with: Medicare Advantage. Robert: From 2024, including 2025.
lines.say: M A PD (Medicare Advantage Prescription Drug plan). What it is: Drug cover built into an M A plan. Used with: Medicare Advantage. Robert: From 2024, including 2025.

lines.raw: The 2025 changes: a $2,000 cap.
lines.say: The 2025 changes: a 2000 dollars cap.

lines.raw: Part D used to have a "**coverage gap**" (often called the **donut hole**) and no firm limit on what people paid.
lines.say: Part D used to have a "coverage gap" (often called the donut hole) and no firm limit on what people paid.

lines.raw: A law passed in 2022 changed this.
lines.say: A law passed in 2022 changed this.

lines.raw: From **2025**, Part D has a simple shape with a hard cap: once a person has paid **$2,000** out of pocket for covered drugs in the year, they pay **$0** for the rest of the year.
lines.say: From 2025, Part D has a simple shape with a hard cap: once a person has paid 2000 dollars out of pocket for covered drugs in the year, they pay 0 dollars for the rest of the year.

lines.raw: The standard Part D design in 2025 (plans can offer lower costs, as Robert's does).
lines.say: The standard Part D design in 2025 (plans can offer lower costs, as Robert's does).

lines.raw: 1. Deductible. What the person pays: The full drug price, up to **$590**. Ends when: $590 has been paid (many plans have a lower or no deductible).
lines.say: 1. Deductible. What the person pays: The full drug price, up to 590 dollars. Ends when: 590 dollars has been paid (many plans have a lower or no deductible).

lines.raw: 2. Initial coverage. What the person pays: About **25%** of the drug price. Ends when: Their out-of-pocket total reaches **$2,000**.
lines.say: 2. Initial coverage. What the person pays: About 25 percent of the drug price. Ends when: Their out-of-pocket total reaches 2000 dollars.

lines.raw: 3. Catastrophic. What the person pays: **$0**. Ends when: The end of the year.
lines.say: 3. Catastrophic. What the person pays: 0 dollars. Ends when: The end of the year.

lines.raw: Imagine a person on a standard Part D plan who needs a drug costing **$1,500 a month**, starting in January 2025.
lines.say: Imagine a person on a standard Part D plan who needs a drug costing 1500 dollars a month, starting in January 2025.

lines.raw: Watch the cap work.
lines.say: Watch the cap work.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: January. Calculation: $590 deductible + 25% of the remaining $910. Pays this month: $817.50. Paid so far: $817.50.
lines.say: January. Calculation: 590 dollars deductible and 25 percent of the remaining 910 dollars. Pays this month: 817 dollars 50 cents. Paid so far: 817 dollars 50 cents.

lines.raw: February. Calculation: 25% of $1,500. Pays this month: $375.00. Paid so far: $1,192.50.
lines.say: February. Calculation: 25 percent of 1500 dollars. Pays this month: 375 dollars. Paid so far: 1192 dollars 50 cents.

lines.raw: March. Calculation: 25% of $1,500. Pays this month: $375.00. Paid so far: $1,567.50.
lines.say: March. Calculation: 25 percent of 1500 dollars. Pays this month: 375 dollars. Paid so far: 1567 dollars 50 cents.

lines.raw: April. Calculation: Only $432.50 left before the cap. Pays this month: $432.50. Paid so far: $2,000.00.
lines.say: April. Calculation: Only 432 dollars 50 cents left before the cap. Pays this month: 432 dollars 50 cents. Paid so far: 2000 dollars.

lines.raw: May to December. Calculation: Cap reached. Pays this month: $0.00. Paid so far: $2,000.00.
lines.say: May to December. Calculation: Cap reached. Pays this month: 0 dollars. Paid so far: 2000 dollars.

lines.raw: Check the maths.
lines.say: Check the maths.
590 dollars and 25 percent × 910 dollars = 590 dollars and 227 dollars 50 cents = 817 dollars 50 cents.
Then 817 dollars 50 cents and 375 dollars and 375 dollars and 432 dollars 50 cents = 2000 dollars exactly.

lines.say: From 2025, out-of-pocket costs for covered Part D drugs are capped at 2000 dollars a year, and the old coverage gap is gone.
